builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FETTUCCINE: Fast and efficient brain-to-text decoding on mobile devices
summary: FETTUCCINE replaces the compute-intensive language-modeling stack used in speech neuroprostheses with a lightweight ASR-derived end-to-end decoder for neural signals, enabling on-device inference with stable latency. The cost is domain specificity: models are trained and finetuned per user on intracortical recordings and require periodic adaptation to neural non-stationarities to retain accuracy across days. It can fail outside its setting because there is no path to applying it to general NLP or LLM serving workloads, and performance depends on invasive neural implants and user-specific calibration data.
rationale: This is a brain-computer interface method for clinical speech prostheses, not an LLM inference, agent, or RAG technique, so it has no production applicability for an AI/ML engineer working on standard language-model systems.

claims.statement: FETTUCCINE replaces the compute-intensive language-modeling stack used in speech neuroprostheses with a lightweight ASR-derived end-to-end decoder for neural signals, enabling on-device inference with stable latency. The cost is domain specificity: models are trained and finetuned per user on intracortical recordings and require periodic adaptation to neural non-stationarities to retain accuracy across days. It can fail outside its setting because there is no path to applying it to general NLP or LLM serving workloads, and performance depends on invasive neural implants and user-specific calibration data.
Decodes attempted speech to text at up to 370x real-time on a commercial mobile device, reaching 4.39% WER on public intracortical speech neuroprosthesis data.
